# MUGEN engine pack work

## When to Use
Installing characters/stages, migrating an old WinMUGEN pack, porting/fixing a screenpack (select screen, lifebars), rebuilding a `select.def` roster, or diagnosing a MUGEN crash on this Windows host.

## Core rule: migrate, don't fix the old engine
- Old **WinMUGEN** (pre-2006, `winmugen.exe`, `alleg40.dll` + DirectX 7) crashes on Win7+ with `0xc0000005` in `alleg40.dll`. Do NOT try to repair it — **move the content into MUGEN 1.1b1** (`mugen.exe`, 2013), which runs natively on Win11.
- 1.1b1 loads WinMUGEN-era chars/stages fine (log line: `Info: <char> loading in pre-1.0 compatible mode`).
- Confirm a real crash vs. a process-check false negative via the event log: `powershell.exe -NoProfile -Command 'Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName="Application"; Id=1000} -MaxEvents 30 | ? { $_.Message -like "*<exe>*" } | select -First 5 | fl TimeCreated,Message'`. A `0xc0000005` for the OLD exe = engine fault; the 1.1b1 `mugen.exe` should have none.

## Layout (1.1b1)
`chars/<folder>/<folder>.def` · `stages/*.def` · `data/mugen.cfg` (holds `motif = ...`) · `data/select.def` (roster) · `data/<motif>/` (screenpack files) · `font/` · `sound/`.

## Install characters from .rar/.zip archives
- Extract with 7-Zip (NOT on PATH — use the full path): `"/c/Program Files/7-Zip/7z.exe" x "arch.rar" -o"chars" -y`. `unzip` IS on PATH for .zip.
- Archives carry a top-level folder = the char folder; extract into `chars/` so it lands as `chars/<name>/`. Watch the `-o` target: it is relative to the cwd — point it at `mugen-1.1b1/chars`, not a stray `chars/` beside the MUGEN folder.
- Two archives differing only by case (`Silvio Santos` vs `SILVIO SANTOS`) COLLIDE on case-insensitive NTFS. If they are genuinely different chars, extract the second to a distinct folder (`chars/<name> MV/`) and reference its `.def` by explicit path in the roster.
- Some archives are FLAT — char files at the archive top level with no folder (e.g. "Madness Mario", "Leo Stronda", "ronaldo", "simba", many pre-2010 chars). Detect with `7z l -slt arch | grep 'Path = '`: the `.def` sits at top level, not `<folder>\.def`. Extract to a temp dir, wrap the top-level entries in a folder named after the `.def` basename (or the char), then move that folder into `chars/`.
- After installing a char, MOVE its archive into the sibling `chars done/` folder — the user files the consumed input archives there, not in `chars to install/`.

## Build select.def from the FOLDERS on disk (ground truth)
Mega-packs ship a `select.def` that lists only a fraction of the chars actually present, with broken entries. Enumerate `chars/*/` folders instead, resolve each one's `.def`, and write a fresh roster. Resolution per folder: `<folder>.def` (case-insensitive match) → bare folder name; else exactly one non-storyboard `.def` → `folder/that.def`; else skip. `ending.def`/`intro.def` are storyboards, not chars. A folder with a second `.def` (e.g. `zero.def` + `zerosvc.def`) uses the folder-matching one.
- Char names with SPACES are fine — the select.def char field is everything up to the first comma.
- Stage field: `random` (picks from `[ExtraStages]`) is the safe default when there's no curated per-char stage.
- `randomselect` on its own line adds a random-select tile. The user wants exactly ONE, at the very END of the roster.
- **MUGEN 1.1b1 has no empty-cell keyword in `select.def`.** A blank line, the word `empty`, and a lone `,` are all parsed as CHARACTER NAMES — each logs `Error reading character file: chars/<x>/<x>.def` (or `chars//.def`) and is skipped, so the grid fills contiguously with no gap. The `empty`/`,` empty-cell keyword exists only in LATER MUGEN builds (screenpacks like Legacy NoZ ship a `select.def` full of `empty` placeholders that silently fail on 1.1b1). To reserve a screenpack's big-portrait (face) areas, do NOT blank cells in select.def — narrow/reposition the grid instead (see Re-grid). A `;`-comment line is ignored (no cell).
- After a bulk install, report a COUNT plus a THEMATIC grouping of the chars (memes/real-life personalities, Chaves/El-Chavo universe, fighting-game/classic MUGEN, Disney/cartoons, anime, Mario/Nintendo, SpongeBob, Pokémon) — the user wants the summary grouped, not just a number. Also order the select.def roster itself by thematic category (franchise/universe), not alphabetically — the user explicitly asked for chars grouped by category in the roster.

## Remove characters
- Removing a char = delete its `chars/<folder>/` AND its `select.def` line. A stale line logs `Error reading character file: chars/<x>/<x>.def` on every launch; a stale folder is harmless but wastes a slot.
- Filter `select.def` by the EXACT char-name field (everything before the first comma), not by regex/substring over the whole line — names collide: `zero` vs `zerox` vs `Zero_Hotaru`; `donramon` vs `don-ramon`; `CAREQUINHA` vs `CAREQUINHAJ/carequinha.def`. A `^zero` regex or bare substring over-matches. For a multi-char removal, filter with a short script using exact set membership: `name = line.split(',', 1)[0].strip()`, `if name in remove_set: skip`. Match against what `select.def` literally contains (case-sensitive; may include a `folder/def.def` path), not what the user typed.
- Same write hygiene as Build/Pitfalls: never redirect `grep -n` into the file. Afterwards verify `grep -cE '^[0-9]+:' data/select.def` == 0, all three section headers remain, then boot-check.

## Port a screenpack (select screen) to 1.1b1
- Copy the old `data/` screenpack files into `data/<motif>/`: `system.def`, `system.sff`/`.snd`, `fight.def`/`.sff`/`.snd`, `fightfx.*`, `select.sff`, the BG/versus/options/gameover/credits files, and any bare-referenced fonts.
- Set `motif = data/<motif>/system.def` in `data/mugen.cfg`.
- Put `select.def` in BOTH `data/` and `data/<motif>/` (field resolution differs; cheap insurance).
- `spr`/`snd`/`fight` in system.def resolve relative to the motif dir; fonts are searched in order: motif/system dir → MUGEN root → `data/` → `font/`. Copy WinMUGEN `.fnt` fonts into `font/` so `font/xxx.fnt` refs resolve.
- Some screenpacks reference assets by MUGEN-ROOT-relative paths (e.g. `title.bgm = data/MENU.ogg` in `[Music]`), so they must be installed as the DEFAULT motif (`data/system.def`), NOT a sub-motif — dropping them in `data/<motif>/` breaks those refs. Grep `system.def` for `data/...` refs to tell which layout the pack expects.

## Lifebar cropping = coordinate-space mismatch (the classic bug)
WinMUGEN screenpacks use a **320×240** localcoord (no `localcoord` line = 320×240 default). The stock 1.1b1 lifebar is authored for **1280×720** (`p1.pos = 590,40`). Pointing a 320×240 screenpack at the stock `fight.def` puts the lifebar off-screen → "healthbar cropped". **Use the screenpack's own `fight.def`** (anchors like `p1.pos = 160,0`), not the stock one. The old lifebar is NOT what crashes the match — verify before swapping it out.

## Re-grid a select screen to fit N characters
Capacity = `rows × columns` in `[Select Info]` of `system.def`. Grid size in the motif's localcoord space: `width = columns×cell.size.x + (columns−1)×cell.spacing`, `height = rows×cell.size.y + (rows−1)×cell.spacing`. Center it with `pos = (localcoord.x−width)/2, (localcoord.y−height)/2`.
- The clean base for a large-portrait roster is the built-in **`big` motif** (`data/big/system.def`): `localcoord=1280,720` and it reuses `../mugen1/system.sff` + `../mugen1/fight.def`, so its localcoord MATCHES the stock lifebar — no cropping. 200 slots = `rows=10, columns=20` at `cell.size=35`, `cell.spacing=5`, centered `pos=242,162`.
- When you change `cell.size`, also rescale `cell.bg.scale`/`cell.random.scale` in proportion: the `big` motif's cell sprite (`cell.bg.spr=150,0`) is ~100px native and ships at `cell.size=50` with `scale=.5`, i.e. scale = cell.size/native_size. Leaving scale stale while shrinking the cell overflows the box.
- `wrapping = 1` lets the cursor wrap around the grid.
- To keep cells out from under a screenpack's big face/portrait panels (top-left/top-right), cut `columns` to the middle band and recenter `pos` so the grid sits BETWEEN the two face offsets (e.g. Legacy NoZ 24-col → `columns=12`, `pos` pushed right; then set `p1.cursor.startcell`/`p2.cursor.startcell` to the new first/last columns). This is the only reliable reserve on 1.1b1. Before cutting, read the real face footprint (`p1.face.offset`/`p2.face.offset` × `face.scale`): a 120×140 face at `.5` scale is only 60×70px in a corner — e.g. LEGACY's faces sit at 45,68 / 1235,68, so the full width is free and columns can be WIDENED instead of cut.
- A 320×240 screenpack cannot show 200 readable cells (its 8px cells are built for ~1000); re-grid a 1280×720 motif instead.
- Purpose-built large-roster screenpacks (228/235/400+ slots): Mugen Archive (`mugenarchive.com/forums/downloads.php?do=cat&id=117-screenpacks`, may need a free account) and OldGamer on Mugen Guild (`network.mugenguild.com/oldgamer/`, direct `.rar` links). Prefer 1.1b1-native 1280×720 packs.

## Verify by launching and reading mugen.log
`mugen.exe` (re)writes `mugen.log` in its own folder on every launch. Read it instead of guessing:
- `Initializing select screen...finding characters...OK` = roster parsed, no errors.
- `Character <x>.def loaded OK` = a char fully loaded; `Opening fight data file data/<motif>/fight.def...OK` = correct lifebar in use.
- `Error loading VictoryBG` is cosmetic (old screenpacks lack the 1.1 `[Victory Screen]` section); ignore it.
- **Quick-VS** tests a match headlessly: `./mugen.exe <p1> <p2> [-s <stage>]` (e.g. `./mugen.exe kfm kfm720 -s kfm`). Omit `-s` if unsure of a stage name; char names with spaces go in quotes.
- Confirm the process is actually running with `tasklist | grep -i mugen` — never `tasklist //FI` (see windows-terminal-ops).

## Pitfalls
- **Never rewrite `select.def` by redirecting `grep -n` / `cat -n` / `nl` output to the file.** The `-n` line-number flag bakes an `N:` prefix into EVERY line, corrupting the `[Characters]`/`[ExtraStages]`/`[Options]` headers → MUGEN crashes at the select screen with "Could not locate Options group / Error finding characters/stages in select.def". To filter lines OUT of select.def use `grep -v` WITHOUT `-n` (e.g. `grep -vE '^name,' select.def > tmp && mv tmp select.def`), or better edit with the `patch` tool. After ANY select.def write, verify: `grep -cE '^[0-9]+:' data/select.def` must print `0`, and `grep -nE '^\[(Characters|ExtraStages|Options)\]' data/select.def` must show all three headers.
- Double-slash `tasklist //FI` / `taskkill //F //IM` report a live process as dead — single slash only (`tasklist | grep`, `taskkill /F /IM mugen.exe`).
- A `.def` filename may not match its folder (e.g. folder `Silvio Santos MV` → `Silvio Santos.def`); always check the actual `.def` name before writing the roster.
- Old screenpacks' logo/intro storyboards can hang or crash the 1.1 engine (the "DJ-VAN" loader is a known point). Disable with `logo.storyboard =` (empty) / `intro.storyboard =` in system.def — they're just splash screens.
- Disable attract/demo mode (`[Demo Mode] enabled = 0`) when a large pack has flaky chars, so the title screen doesn't auto-play random matches and hit a broken one.
- Non-ASCII filenames (accents like `ç`) can mismatch between a stage/char `.def`'s internal `bgmusic = sound/...` reference (often CP1252) and the on-disk name (Unicode), so BGM silently fails. Normalize such filenames to ASCII and fix the `.def` reference to match. Stages' `bgmusic` paths point at the MUGEN-root `sound/` dir, NOT the stage folder — install `.mp3`s into `sound/`, and the `.def`/`.sff` into `stages/` flat.
- SFF **v1.01** chars (most pre-2010 WinMUGEN chars) have no 9000-series portrait sprites in their main SFF, so 1.1b1 auto-generates the select-screen portraits from the LARGEST sprite — often a huge full-body/effect frame (300–2000px) that overflows the CELL and the FACE. The `.def` `portrait = <sff>, <group>, <image>` field sets ONLY the BIG hover/selected portrait (9000,1); the CELL thumbnail is sprite 9000,0 **inside the character's own main SFF** and is drawn at NATIVE size — so a `portrait =` line (even pointing at a separate portrait SFF) can never fix cell overflow. Fix the cell by appending a 9000,0 sprite sized **25×25** (and a 120×140 9000,1) into the main SFF. The cell is drawn at NATIVE size with no scaling, so the cell sprite MUST be 25×25, not 50×50 — a 50×50 sprite fills the 50×50 cell edge-to-edge and overflows. Reference char: `felipe` (main SFF 9000,0 = 25×25, 9000,1 = 121×139). After installing custom portraits, drop a marker file `.portrait-added` in the char folder (content: `9000,0=25x25 9000,1=120x140 <date>`) so later runs can `test -f chars/<folder>/.portrait-added` and skip already-done chars. For AI-generated portraits, request a SQUARE head-and-shoulders portrait on a FLAT MAGENTA (#FF00FF) background in PS1-era 32-bit 2D fighting-game style; key the magenta to transparent, crop the FACE for the 25×25 cell and HEAD+SHOULDERS for the 120×140 big portrait. Batch-install generated images with `scripts/install_ai_portraits.py` (keys magenta, auto-detects the head, crops both sizes, appends 9000,0/9000,1, writes the marker; v2 SFFs auto-skipped). First run `scripts/scan_portraits.py` to list exactly which v1.01 chars need it (9000,0 missing, tiny <20px, or bigger than cell.size — v2 SFFs are auto-skipped), then run `scripts/fix_cell_portraits.py <folder>...`; binary format and procedure in `references/sff-v101-portraits.md`. Narrowing the grid (see Re-grid) only stops the FACE covering cells — it does not shrink the cell thumbnails. Detect SFF version from the byte at offset 15 (after `ElecbyteSpr` + NUL + 3 reserved): `0x01`=v1.01, `0x02`=v2.00.
- Files extracted from `.rar`/`.zip` often carry the Windows READ-ONLY (and hidden) attribute → `PermissionError` when editing `.def`s. Run `attrib -R -H` over the extracted tree before patching files. A HIDDEN-but-not-read-only SFF (attr `0x22` = archive+hidden, no `0x01` read-only bit) can STILL reject `open(path,'wb')` with `PermissionError` while `open(path,'r+b')` succeeds — `os.chmod`/`attrib` won't help because the read-only bit isn't set. When a truncate-mode write fails after clearing read-only, write in-place via `r+b` (`seek(0)` → `write(bytes)` → `truncate()`) instead of `wb`.

# mugen — agent skill for M.U.G.E.N 1.1b1 packs

A [Hermes](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs) / Claude-compatible agent
skill for working with the **M.U.G.E.N 1.1b1** fighting-game engine: installing
characters and stages, porting/fixing screenpacks, rebuilding rosters, and
surgically fixing the two classic select-screen portrait bugs (overflowing cell
thumbnails and huge face previews on SFF v1.01 characters).

## Layout

```
skills/windows/mugen/
├── SKILL.md                         # main instructions (loaded on trigger)
├── references/
│   └── sff-v101-portraits.md        # SFF v1.01 binary format + portrait-append procedure
└── scripts/
    ├── scan_portraits.py            # list chars whose cell portrait is missing/tiny/oversized
    ├── fix_cell_portraits.py        # append a proper 9000,0/9000,1 into a char's main SFF
    └── install_ai_portraits.py      # key/crop AI-generated portraits (magenta bg) into a char SFF
```

The skill follows the standard `skills/<category>/<skill>/SKILL.md` layout (max
two levels under `skills/`), so it is discoverable by `npx skills add` /
skills.sh and by harnesses that scan a repo's `skills/` tree. Reference files
are loaded on demand (they cost nothing until a question needs them); the
scripts are run, not loaded.

## Install

**Hermes** — clone and symlink, or let the skills CLI do it:

```bash
npx skills add https://github.com/fabiomdiniz/mugen-skill --global
```

**Manual** — place the `mugen/` directory (containing `SKILL.md`) under your
skills tree, e.g. `~/.agents/skills/mugen` (skills.sh) or
`.claude/skills/mugen/` (Claude Code / Claude Platform), keeping
`references/` and `scripts/` alongside it.

## What it covers

- Migrating a WinMUGEN pack into MUGEN 1.1b1 (the old engine crashes on Win7+)
- Installing characters/stages from `.rar`/`.zip`, including flat-wrapped and
  case-colliding archives
- Rebuilding `select.def` from the folders actually on disk (not the pack's
  stale roster)
- Porting/re-gridding screenpacks; the lifebar-cropping fix (localcoord mismatch)
- The select-screen **cell** vs **face** portrait system, and fixing SFF v1.01
  chars whose auto-generated portraits overflow the cell or face

## Notes

- Scripts assume Windows (git-bash/MSYS) — that's where MUGEN 1.1b1 runs.
- `scripts/fix_cell_portraits.py` defaults `MUGEN` to a local install path;
  edit the `MUGEN` constant at the top if your install lives elsewhere.
- See `references/sff-v101-portraits.md` for the SFF v1.01 binary format and the
  full append procedure before modifying the scripts.

# SFF v1.01 select-screen portraits: mechanism, binary format, overflow fix

## How 1.1b1 picks the select-screen portraits
- CELL thumbnail = sprite 9000,0 **in the character's main SFF** (the file named by `sprite =` in the `.def`), drawn at NATIVE size — a 460×595 portrait spills over a 50×50 cell. There is no cell-scaling setting in `[Select Info]`.
- FACE (big hover/selected preview) = sprite 9000,1 (system.def `p1.face.spr = 9000,1`), scaled by `p1.face.scale`.
- The `.def` `portrait = <sff>, <g>, <i>` field sets ONLY the big portrait (9000,1). It never changes the cell (MUGEN FAQ: "Except for the big portrait (9000,1), the answer is no"). A separate `*_portrait.sff` referenced via `portrait =` therefore fixes the FACE only.
- A v1.01 SFF missing 9000,0/9000,1 → MUGEN auto-generates both from the LARGEST sprite in that SFF → overflow of cell and face. The only real fix for the CELL is writing a small 9000,0 (and 9000,1) sprite INTO the main SFF. Grid narrowing (SKILL.md Re-grid) only keeps the face from covering cells.
- Standard sizes for THIS pack (LEGACY screenpack, cell.size 50×50): **9000,0 = 25×25** (NOT 50×50 — the cell is drawn at NATIVE size with no scaling, so a 50×50 sprite fills the 50×50 cell edge-to-edge and reads as overflow; 25×25 gives proper margin). Reference char: `felipe` — main SFF 9000,0 = 25×25, 9000,1 = 121×139. 9000,1 = 120×140, axis (0,0) (matches kfm).

## SFF v1.01 binary format (verified by parsing)
Header, 512 bytes:
- 0–11 `ElecbyteSpr\0` signature · 12–15 version (byte 15: 1 = v1.01, 2 = v2.00) · 16 num_groups u32 · 20 num_images u32 · 24 offset of first subfile u32 · 28 a field that *claims* to be the subheader size but is UNRELIABLE (some SFFs store 512 there; real subfile headers are ALWAYS 32 bytes — never trust offset 28) · 32 palette type (1 = shared, 0 = individual).

Subfile = 32-byte header + PCX data, chained as a linked list (NOT contiguous):
- +0 next subfile offset u32 (0 = last) · +4 data length u32 (excluding header) · +8 axis x i16 · +10 axis y i16 · +12 group u16 · +14 image u16 · +16 linked-copy index u16 · +18 palette flag u8 (1 = reuse previous sprite's palette, 0 = own 768-byte palette at the end of the PCX).
- Walk: start at the header's first-subfile offset, follow the next pointers until 0.
- The FIRST subfile in the list is 9000,0 when the SFF already has portraits — sff2png numbers sprites sequentially in linked-list order, so `spr000.png` may be 9000,0, not group 0,0. Never assume the first sprite is the idle pose.

## Portrait source: strip the source sprite's background FIRST
- The source sprite (usually the SFF's largest) is extracted by sff2png with its own palette applied; its palette index 0 = the char's transparent/background colour (commonly MAGENTA 255,0,255, sometimes black). If you scale that sprite as-is, the background colour becomes an opaque box in the portrait ("character with a magenta/black border overflowing the cell").
- Strip it: read the extracted PNG's `getpalette()[0:3]`, then in an RGBA copy set every pixel equal to that colour to alpha 0. THEN fit/scale on a transparent canvas.
- Transparency convention in the generated portrait: palette index 0 IS transparent in MUGEN v1.01. Build the final palette explicitly as `[magenta] + quantize(rgb,255)` palette, map every alpha<128 pixel to index 0 and every other pixel to (quantized index + 1). Do NOT rely on `quantize(256)` luck — it can put a blended edge colour at index 0, leaving the real background opaque.
- Give the fitted content a small margin (fit within cell−4 px, e.g. 46×46 on a 50×50 canvas) so the art doesn't sit flush against the cell edges (read as "overflowing a bit").
- Tiny existing 9000,0 sprites (10×10) render as "no portrait at all" — the same append (rename old to 8999, append a fresh 50×50) fixes them. Scan for 9000,0 < 20px or missing across all v1.01 main SFFs; v2 SFFs (byte 15 = 2) already carry their own 9000 sprites and must be skipped in that scan.

## Appending a portrait sprite to a v1.01 SFF
1. Generate the portrait as 8-bit indexed PNG (PIL: resize to fit the target box, `quantize(256)`).
2. Build the PCX bytes: 128-byte header (0x0A, version 5, RLE=1, 8bpp, xmin/ymin 0, xmax/ymax w−1/h−1, planes=1, bytes-per-line = width rounded up to EVEN, palette-info=1) + per-scanline RLE (runs capped at 63; a byte with top-2-bits set MUST be encoded as a run, even length 1) + `0x0C` marker + 768-byte palette (PIL `getpalette()`).
3. Append the 32-byte subfile header + PCX at EOF (new subfile's next = 0); set the CURRENT last subfile's next pointer to the new offset; bump header num_images (+1 per sprite) and num_groups (recompute distinct groups, counting renames).
4. If an old 9000,0/9000,1 already exists, rewrite its group to 8999 in place (u16 at subfile+12) so it cannot shadow the new sprite — duplicate (group,image) resolution is unspecified.
5. Verify: walk the list and confirm walked count == header num_images (a shortfall means an orphaned subfile = corruption); re-extract with sff2png (should yield the original count + the new sprites, new 9000,0 = the target size); quick-VS the char and require `Character <x>.def loaded OK`; re-run `scripts/scan_portraits.py` and confirm the char is no longer listed.
`scripts/fix_cell_portraits.py <folder>...` performs steps 1–5 for a list of char folders (takes the main SFF from the `.def` `sprite =` field, so subdir SFFs are handled).

## Pitfalls
- Using the header field at offset 28 as the subheader size CORRUPTS the SFF: the bounds check `off + size <= filelen` then stops the linked-list walk one subfile early whenever the last subfile's PCX < size−32 bytes, so the append orphans the true last subfile and the char fails to load. ALWAYS hardcode 32.
- A corrupted-by-append SFF is easiest to restore by copying the original SFF back from the older sibling pack (same chars) and re-running the append correctly — do not hand-repair the linked list.
- sprmake2 (only needed for separate portrait SFFs, which fix the FACE via `portrait =`): its `[Sprite]` lines (`group, image, filename, x, y`) break when the image path contains SPACES ("Sprite: Too few arguments") — put the `.def`, PNGs and `.act` in one workdir and reference bare filenames; pass the output via `-o` (one argv element, spaces fine). Its `[Pal]` section wants an `.act` (768-byte RGB), not a PNG.
- `glob.glob` treats `[ ]` in a folder name as a character class and silently returns nothing — use `os.listdir` + filter for such paths.
- Char `.def` files may write the files section as `Sprite =x.sff` (capital, no spaces) — match with `(?mi)^\s*sprite\s*=\s*([^\r\n;]+)`. A capture like `[^;]+` spans newlines and swallows the rest of the file.
- The face overflow and the cell overflow are TWO different bugs with two different fixes (grid vs SFF append) — a user reporting "portraits still overflowing" after a face fix is now talking about the cell.
